newsitem.title: GERMANY: TENNIS-SABATINI NEVER GOT USED TO LONELINESS OF TENNIS.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SABATINI NEVER GOT USED TO LONELINESS OF TENNIS.

text.p: Gabriela Sabatini, the former world number two who retired from tennis earlier this month, said in a German magazine interview that she once bought a blond wig to escape the pressure and loneliness of fame.
"Often enough I cried when I lost a match, but I could cope with that," the 26-year-old Argentinian told Stern magazine, according to an advance release from Thursday's edition.
"I never got used to how lonely tennis makes you. Most of the time I was on the road, alone in good times as well as bad," she said in the German text of the interview. "I often felt damn lonely."
"In tennis, you have no private life. Once I even bought a blond wig so as not to be recognised."

Sabatini said the hardest thing of all was the difficulty of finding a boyfriend. "I never know if someone wants to get to know me because he's interested in me or just because he fancies being with someone famous," she said.

"The man I dream of should have his own job and be independent, not just attached to me. But if works out that way, then he has no time to accompany me to tournaments...And besides, most men are far too shy to speak to Gabriela Sabatini."
She said it was impossible to have real friendships with other women players and added she was not especially close to world number one Steffi Graf, with whom she won a Wimbledon doubles title.
The winner of the 1990 U.S. Open and 26 other singles titles said she had not picked up a racket since ending her career and did not miss the game or the circuit at all.

"At the moment I'm just enjoying being able to spend a bit of extra time in bed in the mornings and not having to go to bed so early at night," said Sabatini, who plans to launch a new perfume bearing her name and promote a line of bedroom and bathroom linen.
"I haven't quit life, only professional tennis."
